message.content:
A common mistake people make with "it" is using it incorrectly as a pronoun when the antecedent (the noun it refers to) is unclear or ambiguous. For example:

❌ *"When I saw the dog, it was barking."*

This sentence is unclear—does "it" refer to the dog or the person who saw the dog? The meaning depends on context, but without clarification, it can confuse readers.

✅ Better: *"When I saw the dog, it was barking."* (if the dog is barking)  
✅ Better: *"When I saw the dog, I was startled."* (if the person is reacting)

So, the common mistake is **using "it" without a clear antecedent**, leading to ambiguity. To avoid this, make sure the noun "it" refers to is clear and unambiguous.
